Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:115: Our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever has a house of study in his city and does not go there is liable.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:116: One who disputes his teacher's ruling is liable.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:117: And one who renders a halachic decision in his teacher's presence is liable. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Eruvin 63a): Nadav and Avihu did not die for the sin of offering strange fire itself, since their intention was for the sake of a mitzvah — for they said, Behold it is written in the Torah (Leviticus 1:7), "And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar" — even though fire descends from Heaven, it is a mitzvah to also bring some from an ordinary source. But their punishment was because they rendered a halachic decision in the presence of Moses our teacher.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:118: And our Sages of blessed memory said (Avot 5:8): pestilence comes into the world because of the deaths spoken of in the Torah that were not handed over to the court [to be enforced], and because of the produce of the Sabbatical year. They further said: at four periods pestilence increases — in the fourth year, in the seventh, at the end of the seventh, and at the end of the festival [of Sukkot] each year. In the fourth year, because of the tithe for the poor of the third year [not given properly]; in the seventh, because of the tithe for the poor of the sixth year; at the end of the seventh, because of the produce of the Sabbatical year; and at the end of the festival each year, because of the robbing of the gifts due to the poor. And from this we see that there is death at the hand of Heaven for robbing the gifts due to the poor. And know and consider from this the severity of one who vows charity and does not pay it; and likewise one who shuts his hand from his poor brother and hides himself from his own flesh resembles these, for since he has become obligated to give, he is like one who robs his own [pledged] gifts.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:119: The Seventh Level – the Severity of Excision (Karet): the iniquities for which deliberate transgression incurs excision are those for which one is liable, if committed inadvertently, to bring a sin-offering. And so our Sages of blessed memory said: a person is obligated to bring a sin-offering only for a matter whose deliberate transgression is punished with excision. And the excision is that both he and his offspring are cut off, as it is said (Leviticus 20:20), "they shall bear their sin; they shall die childless."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:120: And liability for excision falls into two categories. The first category is those cut off from this world alone — such as one who has relations with his sister, his father's sister, his mother's sister, his wife's sister, or his brother's wife after her divorce or after her husband's death; and likewise one who has relations with his father's brother's wife or his mother's brother's wife; and one who eats forbidden fat or blood; and one who eats chametz on Passover; and one who performs labor on Yom Kippur; and one who failed to bring the Passover offering; and one who has relations with a menstruant woman.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:121: And the second category is those cut off from both this world and the World to Come — such as one who worships idols, one who commits transgressions publicly, one who scorns the Torah (such as one who demeans those who study it and those who love the Blessed Name), and one who breaks the covenant of the flesh [circumcision]. And we shall explain the matter of those factions well at the Eleventh Level.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:122: And one who has become liable to excision may sometimes have his merit extended in this world for two or three generations, for the delay of death for the wicked serves to pay them their reward in this world, so as to destroy them from the World to Come, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them; he will not delay for one who hates him, he will repay him to his face." And the matter is explained in the words of David the king, peace upon him (Psalms 92:7-8), "A brutish man knows not, nor does a fool understand this: when the wicked spring up like grass, and all the workers of iniquity flourish, it is that they may be destroyed forever." And so Asaph, peace upon him, said (Psalms 73:3-4,17), "For I was envious of the boastful... for there are no bonds in their death... until I entered the sanctuaries of God, then I understood their end." Its meaning: the vengeance upon the wicked comes in their latter end, as it is said (Proverbs 24:20), "For there shall be no future for the evil man; the lamp of the wicked shall be put out."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:123: And our Sages of blessed memory said: Rabbi Yoshiah said, for three reasons the Holy One, blessed be He, is patient with the wicked in this world: perhaps they will do teshuvah; or they performed mitzvot for which the Holy One, blessed be He, will pay them their reward in this world; or perhaps righteous sons will emerge from them — for so we find, that when patience was shown to Ahaz, Hezekiah emerged from him; and Amon too, Josiah emerged from him; and Shimi too, Mordechai emerged from him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:124: And the matter of excision is the shortening of years, as it is said (Proverbs 10:27), "but the years of the wicked shall be shortened." And regarding the shortening of years there is a distinction between death and excision: for excision means dying before the age of fifty, while death [as a separate category of punishment] means dying before sixty, like those who died in the wilderness. Its meaning: one who was decreed to live seventy or eighty years, and became liable to death, will die under the age of sixty; but there are righteous men whose number of days is less than sixty — as they said, fifty-two years was the death of Samuel of Ramah. And it is said (Numbers 4:18), "Do not cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites," and our Sages of blessed memory expounded from this that excision means dying before the age of fifty. The meaning of the verse: let there be no cause from you to cut off the tribe of the Kohathites from the service of the Levites — for if you do not guard them so that they do not come to look, as it were, upon the swallowing of the holy things, they will be cut off from the service of the Levites and will die before the age of fifty, as it is said (Numbers 8:25), "and from the age of fifty years he shall return from the service of the work, etc."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:125: And among those liable to excision is one who brings a wicked snare and corruption upon his offspring, beyond merely cutting off the future of his own line — namely, one who has relations with a menstruant woman. And that offspring is called "seed of evildoers," for the mark of brazenness will be upon his forehead throughout his life, as our Sages of blessed memory said: a brazen person is surely the son of a menstruant woman. And the iniquities of the son fall upon the bones of the father, for he has brought calamity upon his own soul, causing his child to be a transgressor from the womb; and woe to the wicked man, for he has brought ruin upon himself, and his own soul and his wife's soul shall surely be cut off, and his whole worthless offspring is cut off. And the woman remains in the impurity of her menstruation even if she has become pure from her flow and counted her seven days according to the law, as long as she has not immersed in a spring of water, or river water, or a gathering of water containing forty se'ah — the numerical value (gematria) of which corresponds to the word "at," "slowly" [an allusion the author draws].
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:126: The Eighth Level – the Four Death Penalties of the Court: these are stoning, burning, decapitation, and strangulation. Stoning is more severe than burning, burning more severe than decapitation by sword, and decapitation more severe than strangulation. Among the transgressions punished by stoning are: one who has relations with his father's wife, with his daughter-in-law, or with a male; a necromancer or sorcerer; one who desecrates the Sabbath; one who curses his father or mother; one who has relations with a betrothed young woman; one who entices others to idolatry; a sorcerer; and a rebellious son. And more severe than all of these are the blasphemer and the idol-worshipper.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:127: By burning: one who has relations with a woman and her daughter, or her husband's daughter, or her son's daughter, or her daughter's daughter, or his mother-in-law, or his mother-in-law's mother, or his father-in-law's mother.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:128: By the sword — two: the murderer, and the inhabitants of a city led astray to idolatry.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:129: By strangulation: one who strikes his father or mother; one who kidnaps a fellow Israelite; an elder who defies the ruling of the court; a false prophet; one who prophesies in the name of idolatry; and one who has relations with a married woman.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:130: Our Sages of blessed memory said (Ketubot 30a): from the day the Holy Temple was destroyed, even though the four death penalties of the court were suspended, the judgment of the four death penalties was not suspended. One liable to stoning either falls from a roof or is trampled by a wild animal; one liable to burning either falls into a fire or is bitten by a snake; one liable to decapitation is set upon by bandits; and one liable to strangulation either drowns in a river or dies of croup.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:131: And one who has relations with a gentile bondwoman resembles those liable to the death penalties of the court in two ways, for our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 81b): one who has relations with an Aramean woman, zealots may attack him — as it is written (Numbers 25:8), "and he pierced the two of them." And the explanation of the matter is that if a man finds him thus straying in a place where he can be seen, and he has not yet separated from the transgression, whoever encounters him at that moment may put him to death. And this matter is more severe than all liable to the death penalties of the court, for they are not put to death except by witnesses and forewarning and by the ruling of the Sanhedrin, while this sinner may be killed by whoever finds him, without witnesses or forewarning.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:132: And beyond this, the wicked man just mentioned has profaned the holiness of the Lord, whom he loved, and has had relations with the daughter of a foreign god; and every foreign child that he fathers will become for him a snare and a stumbling-block, a perpetual reminder of the iniquity; the father will bear the iniquity of the son, and he has betrayed the Lord, for he has fathered strange children.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:133: And further: Heaven will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him, for his sin will hasten his own downfall, and his end will be to be hanged by the crown of his head upon a tree. And behold, in this he resembles those liable to the death penalties of the court in the time after the destruction of the Temple, in that Heaven shall judge that they die in their own rebellion, not as other men die, as we have explained. And so our Sages said: whoever has relations with a gentile bondwoman is hanged by the crown of his head, as it is said (Psalms 68:22), "But God shall smite the head of His enemies, the hairy crown of one who continues in his guilty ways." Its meaning: He shall smite the crown by the hair, for he will be hanged by his own hair. And it is said (Malachi 2:12), "May the Lord cut off, for the man who does this, one who awakens and one who answers from the tents of Jacob" — and our Sages explained (Sanhedrin 82a): "one who awakens" refers to the sages, "and one who answers" refers to the students.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:134: And our Sages of blessed memory said (Avot 5:8): the sword comes into the world for the delay of justice, for the perversion of justice, and for those who render halachic decisions not in accordance with the law; a wild beast comes into the world for a false oath and for the desecration of the Name.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:135: And among the matters that it would be pleasant for those who rebuke to warn about and testify concerning to the people, and to guard against the ways of the reckless, is the commandment of the Sabbath — the primary categories of forbidden labor and their sub-categories — for many of these have escaped the notice of the many, with no one to tell, no one to make it heard.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:136: The Ninth Level – the Severity of the Transgressions for Which One Must Die Rather Than Transgress: our Sages of blessed memory said (Sanhedrin 74a): for all the transgressions in the Torah, if a man is told, Transgress and do not be killed, he should transgress and not be killed, as it is said (Leviticus 18:5), "which a man shall do and live by them" — "live by them," and not that he should die by them — except for idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed, for which, if a man is told to transgress one of these three or be killed, he should be killed and not transgress. And this applies even if they tell him to commit the transgression privately; and if they tell him to transgress any of the commandments of the Torah publicly, he should be killed and not transgress, as it is said (Leviticus 22:32), "and I will be sanctified among the children of Israel."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:137: And even the lighter aspect of these three mentioned transgressions carries a punishment more severe than that of many grave transgressions; and our Sages of blessed memory called the lighter aspect of a transgression "the dust of the transgression." And they said: one may be healed with anything from an illness involving danger to life, except with wood from an asherah tree — for if they tell him, Bring leaves of an asherah and be healed by them, he should die rather than be healed by them. And even though one who merely benefits from the wood of an asherah is not thereby worshipping idolatry, since it is the dust of idolatry, he should die rather than be healed by it, since this is like strengthening the hands of those who worship the asherah, lest they say, The asherah saved him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:138: And likewise concerning sexual immorality: if a man desired a married woman, and they told him, There is no cure for your affliction unless she stands naked before you, or converses with you — he should die rather than breach the fence of the prohibition against a married woman. And from this you may recognize the severity of mere physical contact with a married woman's hand.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:139: And behold, the dust of murder is causing another's face to turn white [with shame], for his face grows pale and the ruddy color flees, resembling murder; and so our Sages of blessed memory said. And the second reason: the pain of being shamed is more bitter than death; therefore our Sages of blessed memory said, a man should always throw himself into a fiery furnace rather than shame his fellow publicly. And they did not say this concerning other grave transgressions; indeed, they likened the dust of murder to murder itself, and just as they said one should be killed rather than murder, so likewise they said one should throw himself into a fiery furnace rather than shame his fellow publicly. And they derived this from the matter of Tamar, as it is said (Genesis 38:25), "When she was brought forth, she sent to her father-in-law, etc." — behold, even though they had brought her out to be burned, she did not reveal that she was pregnant by Judah, so as not to shame him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:140: They further said: all who descend to Gehinnom eventually ascend, except three, who descend and do not ascend: one who shames his fellow publicly; one who calls his fellow by a demeaning nickname; and one who has relations with a married woman. Behold, they have likened one who shames his fellow publicly and one who calls his fellow a demeaning nickname — since this too shames his face — to one who has relations with a married woman, which is among the transgressions for which one should be killed rather than transgress.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:141: They further said: one who shames his fellow publicly has no share in the World to Come. And the reason they did not say this of the murderer, that he has no share in the World to Come (the explanation being that since the shaming is merely an offshoot of murder, as stated above, that it is the "dust" of murder, the murder itself is not lesser than the shaming, and yet they did not say of it that he has no share in the World to Come) — is that one who shames his fellow does not recognize the greatness of his sin, and his soul is not bitter over his iniquity as is the murderer's; therefore he is far from teshuvah.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:142: And concerning the commandment of the Sabbath, our Sages of blessed memory said (Jerusalem Talmud, Nedarim 3:9): the Sabbath is weighed as equal to all the commandments. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Chullin 5a) that one who worships idols, or who desecrates the Sabbath publicly, is an apostate regarding the whole Torah, his ritual slaughter is deemed carrion, and he renders wine forbidden by his touch.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:143: The Tenth Level – the Severity of the Transgressions for Which the Transgressor Has No Share in the World to Come: all creatures were created for the glory of the Blessed Name, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "everyone that is called by My name and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him." Indeed, it is known from reason that one who desecrates the Name and scorns His word has lost his hope, for it is not enough for him that he fails to fulfill what is demanded of him from the very essence of his creation — to honor the Name and sanctify it — but he has stretched forth his hand to do the opposite and the reverse, to profane His holy Name. And so it is written (Numbers 15:30), "But the soul that acts presumptuously (with a high hand)... reviles the Lord, and that soul shall be cut off from among his people. Because he has despised the word of the Lord and has broken His commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him" — for death does not atone for him and he has no share in the World to Come. Therefore Scripture mentions here "his iniquity shall be upon him," for it does not say this concerning other cases of excision. And the meaning of "the soul that acts with a high hand" is one who commits transgressions publicly known to people; and likewise one who casts off the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, even in secret, for he too acts with a high hand. And the matter of casting off the yoke is such as an apostate who eats carrion, or eats forbidden fat and blood, or desecrates festivals — even though he does not transgress the other commandments, since he has removed from himself the yoke of one single warning, he has already rebelled against the exalted Name. It is true that even the righteous sometimes stumble in a single sin, but this is only by way of chance, when the inclination overpowers them, and their soul is bitter to them over the matter, and they are careful of it afterward; but one who says in his heart that he intends to cast off from himself the yoke of a single warning, every time he desires to transgress it, is the one called "an apostate regarding one thing," and we have already stated this earlier, in the First Gate of Teshuvah. And they said: shepherds [who graze animals on others' land] are neither lifted up from the pit nor lowered into it. And the matter of shepherds is: men who graze their cattle in others' fields, casting off from themselves the yoke of the prohibition against robbery — and their status is like that of the apostate who eats carrion or any other transgression out of appetite; but heretics and unbelievers are lowered into the pit. And the apostate who eats carrion out of spite is also included among the heretics; and the matter of "out of spite" is that he does not sin for the desire of appetite for food, for even when there is properly slaughtered meat before him, he will take from the carrion — since he is a rebel and does not accept upon himself to guard against the prohibition of carrion.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:144: Behold, we have explained the matter of "the soul that acts with a high hand." Now let us explain "he has despised the word of the Lord." Our Sages of blessed memory said: "he has despised the word of the Lord and has broken His commandment" — this refers to one who says there is no Torah from Heaven, and one who interprets the Torah with a brazen face, and one who demeans Torah scholars, and one who demeans the festivals — for even if he possesses Torah and good deeds, he has no share in the World to Come.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:145: And the meaning of "one who interprets the Torah with a brazen face" is a man who has been brazen enough to speak of the Torah things that are not so, saying that these verses and these narratives were written in the Torah for no reason, and out of his pride and arrogance says in his heart — since his own grasp does not reach the true nature of the meaning of the words — that there is no hidden depth to them. And it is said (Deuteronomy 32:47), "for it is no empty thing for you." And our Sages of blessed memory said (Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah 4:1): if it seems empty, it is because of you — meaning, because you do not know how to explain the reason of the matter. And likewise anyone who abandons a single teaching among the words of the Torah and does not acknowledge it — behold, this too is interpreting the Torah with a brazen face, such as one who says, What benefit have we gained from those who study the Torah? — if they became wise, they became wise for their own sake, and we have received no inheritance from their reward. Behold, such a person has denied what is written in the Torah (Genesis 18:26), "and I will forgive the whole place for their sake."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:146: And the matter of one who demeans the festivals is one who performs labor on the intermediate days of a festival, and scorns the punishment because the prohibition of labor on the intermediate days of a festival is not explicitly stated in the Torah; and this is in the manner of the apostate regarding one thing out of spite, which we have already explained has no share in the World to Come. And our Sages of blessed memory said: if one came to convert and said, Behold, I accept upon myself the whole Torah except for one item among the words of the Sages, he is not to be accepted. And they said, of blessed memory (Makkot 23a): one who demeans the festivals is as though he worshipped idols, as it is said (Exodus 34:17-18), "You shall not make molten gods for yourselves," and immediately following, "The feast of unleavened bread you shall keep." And our Sages explained: "the feast of unleavened bread you shall keep" means that you shall not perform labor throughout the whole feast of unleavened bread; and we have been warned by this concerning the labor of the intermediate days of a festival. And what is written, "On the first day a Sabbath-rest, and on the seventh day a Sabbath-rest," [teaches] that there are many labors permitted on the intermediate days of a festival, as they are explained in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:147: And this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 99b): that one who demeans Torah scholars scorns the word of the Lord and has no share in the World to Come — this matter has a root in reason and a foundation in inquiry, and we shall now set out for you the matter with good sense and knowledge. Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 3:35), "The wise shall inherit honor, but fools carry off shame (kalon)." The matter of "kalon" is a "man of shame," in the sense of (Psalms 109:4), "but I am prayer" [meaning "a man of prayer"], and (Jeremiah 9:4[5]), "your dwelling is in the midst of deceit" [meaning "in the midst of deceitful men"]. Its meaning: the demeaned and vile man lifts up fools and honors and praises them, for there are great benefits in the honor shown to the wise and the upright, and many mighty stumbling-blocks in the honor shown to fools and the wicked — for when the wise are honored and made eminent, their words are heeded, and all the people will attach themselves to them and pattern themselves after their counsel. And the second reason: when people see all their honor, they will learn a lesson to inherit honor themselves, and knowledge will increase. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Pesachim 50b): a man should always occupy himself with Torah even not for its own sake, for from doing so not for its own sake, he comes to do so for its own sake. And the third reason: many of slumbering heart will awaken from their sleep upon seeing the splendor of the honor of the Torah, and they will recognize its worth, and desire for it will come into their hearts, and their occupation with it will be for the sake of the exalted Name and to serve Him with a whole heart.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:148: Behold, these are honorable reasons, firm as a molten mirror; but there is yet another honorable reason surpassing all of them, to which we alluded in the opening of our words concerning the matter of the evil factions mentioned. For it is a known matter that among the ways of sanctifying the Blessed Name is to make known, in every utterance of the lips and every hint of the eyes and every conduct and deed of the hands, that the foundation of a man's soul, and the beauty of his ornament, and the good, the essential, the beneficial and the precious thing within him, is the service of the Blessed Name, His fear, and His Torah — as it is written, "for this is the whole of man." And this matter is the honor of the Blessed Name; and those who demean Torah scholars and His fear nullify this knowledge and display the opposite in their conduct, and it is as though they were saying, in effect, that the service [of God] is not essential, that honor and glory belong to the success of worldly matters, and that the root of the matter can be found without the service of the Blessed Name — and they thereby desecrate the Torah. Therefore let them perish from the midst of the assembly, and let their claim come to nothing though they say with their mouths that they serve the Lord without occupation in Torah. Is it not known that the service [of God] cannot endure except through those who study the Torah, who meditate on it day and night? For they teach knowledge and are those who understand the times, to know what Israel should do, and they establish it in Israel so that it not be forgotten from the mouths of their offspring; and in a place where there are no students of Torah, stumbling-blocks multiply and there is no uprightness in man. Therefore the servants of the Blessed Name should honor the sages of Torah for the honor of the Blessed Name, and to make known that His service alone is the essential thing to be found. And since it has become clear that the Blessed Name created everything for His glory, a person is obligated to set his heart at all times to honor the Lord and sanctify Him in all his words, and to exalt Him, to thank Him and bless Him continually, as it is said (Psalms 34:2), "I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth." And when he stands among the people and speaks with his companions, he should consider carefully and be precise and watch over every utterance of his lips, to sanctify the Lord in his words, and to speak in praise of His service and the glory of His fear, and to praise those who serve Him and fear Him — and by this he will merit, through the meditation of his heart and the utterance of his lips, without labor or the deed of his hands, a great merit reaching unto heaven, for this is among the essential purposes of man's creation. And it is said (Proverbs 27:21), "The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; and a man is according to his praise." Its meaning: a man's own worth is judged by what he praises. If he praises good deeds, the wise, and the righteous, you shall know and recognize that he is a good man and that the root of righteousness is found in him, for he would not find it in his heart to praise the good and the good people continually in all his words, and to condemn transgressions and demean their perpetrators, unless he loathed evil and chose good. And even if it is possible that he has hidden iniquities of his own, he is nevertheless among those who love righteousness, and has a root in his own choice, and is among the company of those who honor the Lord. But one who praises shameful deeds, or praises the wicked, is himself utterly wicked and one who desecrates the service of the Blessed Name.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:149: Solomon the king, peace upon him, further said (Proverbs 25:26-27), "A troubled spring and a corrupted fountain is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked. To eat too much honey is not good, so to search too much into their own glory is glory." For just as when a man muddies a spring with his feet, its waters become turbid for the moment, but afterward the water settles and becomes as clear as before — so is the righteous man: when he gives way before the wicked, his own rank is not thereby lowered or diminished, and if he is troubled for the moment — "a righteous man falls seven times and rises" — he shall return to his strength and his glory. "To eat too much honey is not good" — but to search abundantly into the glory of the righteous is glory to the one who searches, for the righteous is mentioned in the verse above, and the word "too much" is drawn forward to apply to "searching into their glory," as is the rule in many places [of Scripture]. And the stumbling-blocks found in honoring the wicked are many and well known, for their honor involves the desecration of Torah and of [God's] service, and this is an iniquity that consumes from soul to flesh.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:150: And the second reason: for many are drawn after them and cling to their deeds.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:151: And the third reason: those who associate with them, even though they do not act as they do, receive punishments just like them, as we have already mentioned.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:152: And the fourth reason: they suppress the honor of men of truth and nullify the [true] service, and there is no success for the honor of the righteous except after the lowering of the honor of the wicked, as it is written (Proverbs 14:11), "The house of the wicked shall be destroyed, but the tent of the upright shall flourish," and it is said (Proverbs 11:11), "By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is overthrown."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:153: Our Sages of blessed memory further said (Berachot 24a): included in what is written, "he has despised the word of the Lord," is one who speaks words of Torah in filthy alleyways, and whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not do so, and one who reads the books of heretics. And what is written, "and has broken His commandment," refers to one who breaks the covenant of the flesh.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:154: We have further learned: all of Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it is said (Isaiah 60:21), "And your people, all of them righteous, shall inherit the land forever." And these are they who have no share in the World to Come: one who says that the resurrection of the dead is not [derived] from the Torah, one who says the Torah is not from Heaven, and the heretic (apikoros). And our Sages of blessed memory warned us in this teaching to believe that the belief in the resurrection of the dead is written in the Torah, and that it is one of its foundations. And one of the places where the resurrection of the dead is explained in the Torah is where it is said (Deuteronomy 32:39), "I put to death and I bring to life; I have wounded, and I heal." And our Sages of blessed memory said (Pesachim 68a): one might think that death is with one [generation] and resurrection with another; Scripture therefore teaches, "I have wounded, and I heal" — just as the wounding and the healing are of the same one, so too the death and the resurrection are of the same one.
